statement: Submodule advancement MUST retain published contributor history, admit only descendant pins, and distinguish an unread supplier from a current supplier.
because: Leader, 2026-10-11: Goal: NO DIVERGENCE, and perfect use of github for CI/CD, handling of our code fabrication and deployment into publication.
consumer: 561-group/bare-cedar-fog and the section repositories hiring the reusable sync workflows

specification.output: one pull request retaining the existing sync branch and checked-out base history with only proven descendant pin changes
refusals: non-gitlink, deleted, ambiguous or supplier-definition base conflict
specification.baseConflictReceiving: A conflicting base merge may select only the descendant of two comparable gitlink stages, each proven to descend from their recorded common stage. Require exactly one merge base and an exact original-stage match. In the common base, both sides and the clean merge index, every conflicting path must retain one identical supplier section name and all configured values, including URL, path, branch and ref metadata. Reject deleted, renamed, ambiguous or changed conflicting identities, unresolved definitions and definition-file type or mode changes. Unrelated clean supplier additions remain ordinary preserved merge content. Qualify every conflict before staging any resolution; retain both parent histories and unrelated clean merge changes. Abort and publish nothing when any condition is unresolved.
specification.publication: ordinary fast-forward push followed by authoritative ref readback; never a force push
specification.ancestryObservation: Request GitHub compare page 2 with per_page=1 to exclude file patches while retaining comparison-wide status, ahead/behind counts and merge-base identity. Require exact input SHAs, matching comparison URL and base SHA, and consistent aggregate counts and ancestor identity. An empty commit page is valid for a small, identical or behind comparison; never infer ancestry from page contents. Keep child output bounded to 1 MiB and return unknown for malformed, foreign, contradictory, oversized or failed observations without retrying an unbounded patch response. GitHub pagination contract: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/commits#compare-two-commits
specification.callerReceiving: A root sync caller with submodules and no parent runs its existing advance job after a reviewed change to .github/workflows/sync.yml reaches its declared default branch. Preserve dispatch, nightly scheduling, manual invocation, runner, token, permissions and concurrency. Parent/child callers retain their existing push notification semantics. Review-branch source updates must not trigger the default-branch caller activation.
specification.pendingReviewReceiving: Derive the complete pending gitlink proposal from the exact checked-out base to the published review head, including prior advances still awaiting integration. Require base ancestry, unchanged supplier definitions, descendant pins and no unrelated or unsupported pending tree changes. Preserve contributor history, but refuse automated pin-only metadata for manual source changes. A run with no new commit still receives pending metadata without another push. Bind metadata to exact live base/head refs and the unique same-repository open pull request before writing and read back the body and both refs afterward. Lookup failures, ambiguity, stale refs and mismatched review identities prevent writes. Reconcile a lost PATCH or POST response at the original destination without replay or duplicate creation; unread or nonmatching results stay unresolved. Empty pending trees create no review. Delete stale local metadata before each run. The reusable workflow must select the qualified immutable engine revision, and the caller must be regenerated through its existing source receiver before actual consumer acceptance.

design: Receive the existing branch and checked-out base before computing pin changes in the existing advance engine. Publish through the shared reusable workflows; gitlinks remain the parent source references. Machine deployment is a separate receiving operation.
metadataTrustBoundary: The maintained advance engine qualifies the complete local Git trees and writes the local proposal in .git; the metadata receiver consumes that same-run engine output and validates its exact base/head suffix and live destination. It does not independently prove arbitrary caller-supplied proposal bodies or supplier trees. Live ref and PR readbacks detect observed races and unknown results; GitHub pull-request body updates provide no cross-ref compare-and-swap, so this is not an atomic write guarantee. Even an unchanged-body result requires a fresh exact-review read and final ref reads.
activation: Receive and qualify the source engine and metadata receiver first while retaining the existing workflow unchanged. In a later reviewed activation, bind the reusable workflow's engine checkout to that immutable received source commit and change the pending gate and metadata invocation together. Never combine the new pending gate with an old engine that emits only advanced. Regenerate and receive the hiring caller through the existing source generator; verify a later real cumulative and unchanged-head run at the selected workflow and engine identities before claiming consumer acceptance.
receiving: Observe real supplier heads and ancestry against parent gitlinks; inspect the shared service PR and the parent's generated caller and mounted owner. A package check alone does not establish source or deployment convergence.
